Thanks again for the demo last week. Our SIG reviewer had a few follow-up questions focused on Dedicated GPU isolation for multi-tenant workloads before we can sign off:

- How do you prevent residual KV cache or model-state from being visible to a subsequently scheduled tenant (memory reuse between contexts)?
- When MIG is not available (older hardware), what kernel/driver/runtime controls do you rely on to guarantee separation?
- Can you describe eviction behavior under high memory pressure and how you ensure no cross-tenant leakage during a context switch?
- Any artifacts you can provide: short trace/log excerpt, diagram of runtime boundaries, or a short attestation for the SIG?

Hi team —

Below are concrete controls and an example timeline. Ill attach a log snippet that illustrates the eviction/re-assignment sequence.

Key controls (brief):
- Hardware-assisted partitioning: when A100/A30 with MIG is available we assign tenants to separate MIG instances. That provides hardware PT (page table) and L2 cache isolation.
- Driver/runtime segregation: on non-MIG hosts we run a per-tenant model process inside an isolated Linux container with GPU exclusive mode and cgroup controls for PCI device access. Before assigning the GPU to a new tenant we explicitly zero-device memory pages via driver APIs (kernel call chain shown in runbook).
- KV cache segmentation: each tenant has a namespaced KV cache. Eviction is per-namespace; cache keys include tenant-id prefixes so theres no cross-tenant lookup. Cache lifecycle: populate -> active TTL -> soft-evict -> free.
- Eviction policy & proof points: when memory pressure crosses a threshold we preempt the oldest low-priority contexts, flush their KV namespace to ephemeral storage only if required (never to shared persistent cache), and run a zeroing pass before re-allocation.

Example timeline (simplified):
1) 10:02:14 — tenant A allocated context, KV namespace created (namespace: tenant-A/ctx-117)
2) 10:17:03 — system detects memory watermark breach (85%) and marks ctx-117 for preemptive eviction
3) 10:17:05 — ctx-117 checkpointed (in-memory metadata only), KV namespace soft-evicted; no keys promoted to shared cache
4) 10:17:06 — driver zeroing pass initiated on GPU pages previously used by ctx-117 (driver log id: ZP-8392)
5) 10:17:09 — tenant B allocation begins; driver confirms zeroed allocation before mapping

I attach a compact log excerpt showing the ZP-8392 zeroing event and the KV cache namespace eviction markers. Also attaching the isolation diagram Naomi mentioned.

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
